sections.heading: EPDM Roof Repair or EPDM Roof Replacement?

c.v: An EPDM roof repair fits local damage; an EPDM roof replacement fits a worn-out membrane.

runs.v: A full replacement, starting with a tear off of the existing roof, follows when seam failures recur or water soaks the insulation. With proper maintenance, EPDM lasts 15 to 30 years in Newark: it withstands freeze-thaw cycles and is highly resistant to UV exposure and weathering, the environmental conditions that attack seams first. Regular inspections extend its life: clear drains, check laps, and remove debris.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing installs and repairs EPDM rubber membrane on residential flat and low-slope roofs across Essex County: row-house roofs, rear extensions, porches, and garages.

runs.v: Repairing or replacing the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family dwelling is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, needing no construction permit.

Small roofs are usually fully adhered, and EPDM's wide sheets often cover a porch or garage with no field seam. Row-house roofs share a parapet with the neighbor, so party-wall flashings need the most care. Black EPDM over a top-floor bedroom runs warm; added insulation or white EPDM can improve energy efficiency.

sections.heading: What Are the Downsides of EPDM Rubber Roofing?

c.v: EPDM rubber roofing has four weaknesses.

runs.v: Black EPDM's heat absorption warms rooms below, while white membranes reflect UV rays and lower cooling costs. Glued laps are the weak point: seam failures are the most common issue. Foot traffic and branches puncture rubber. Aging membranes shrink at flashings. Strengths: UV resistance, cold-weather flexibility, long-term performance, and recyclability; some membranes contain recycled content.

faqs.q: How long does an EPDM rubber roof last in Essex County?

runs.v: EPDM lasts 15 to 25 years, per InterNACHI, and a well-maintained roof can last 20 to 30 years.

faqs.q: What is the difference between EPDM and TPO for a flat roof?

runs.v: Both are single-ply membranes: EPDM is rubber with glued or taped seams, while TPO has heat-welded seams and a shorter 7-to-20-year life.

faqs.q: Can an EPDM rubber roof be repaired instead of replaced?

runs.v: Yes, when damage stays local; replace it at the end of its service life or when seam and flashing failures spread.

faqs.q: How much does rubber roofing EPDM cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Repair in the Newark area runs $300–$1,100 for a typical job and NJ installation $7.00–$10.00 per square foot; Newark Quality Roofing provides a free written estimate.

faqs.q: Why does an EPDM roof leak at the seams?

runs.v: Seam adhesive breaks down before the rubber does; shrinkage at edges and penetrations comes second.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof repair in Newark require a permit?

runs.v: Not on a detached one- or two-family home (ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7), but repairing more than 25% of a commercial building's roof in 12 months requires a permit.

faqs.q: Is EPDM used for commercial roofing on commercial buildings?

runs.v: Yes: EPDM is a preferred choice for low-slope commercial roofs, commonly chosen for commercial and multi-family properties in New Jersey, and installed fully adhered, mechanically attached, or ballasted.
Manufacturers sell EPDM through roofing supply distributors, mostly to contractors; home centers stock small rolls, but most property owners buy it installed.
